title: canary-rollout-scratchpad-emma-zhou
body:
Quick scratchpad for upcoming canary rollout (hosted API) — notes to self + checklist. Mostly rough, will extract formal checklist later.

Context:
- Target: deploy redwood-model-v2.1-quant to hosted-prod (us-west-2) as primary generation backend for /v1/generate route.
- Current prod stable: redwood-model-v1.9 (baseline).
- Motivation: v2.1 gives ~15% cost per-token improvement in perf tests and slightly lower latency at p50 for 256 tokens. Need to validate generation quality for existing prompt sets.

High-level plan (canary policy):
- Phase 0 (prechecks): infra + smoke tests in staging, verify metrics collection, validate fallback hook.
- Phase 1 (internal canary): 1% of traffic, only internal org tokens + regression eval set. 24h.
- Phase 2 (gradual ramp): 5% -> 10% -> 25% over 48–72h if green.
- Phase 3 (broad canary): 50% for 24h with randomized user sample, additional lexicon/regression checks.
- Phase 4 (full): 100% and unpin older version from default route.

Traffic routing specifics:
- Use rollout policy: header-based for internal canary (X-Redwood-Canary: true) and probabilistic routing for public canary.
- Config: canary-weights config stored in rollout service: start=0.01 -> 0.05 -> 0.10 -> 0.25 -> 0.5 -> 1.0 (steps can be paused).
- K8s: Deployment uses modelvariant label; ensure hostAffinity to dedicated GPU pool for v2.1.

Version pinning notes:
- Do not change default pinned version in tenant config until Phase 4. Pinning should remain explicit per-route: /v1/generate -> redwood-model-v1.9 until full release.
- Canary routes created as: route:generate:canary:v2.1 (isolated config, logs forwarded to canary-index).
- Compatibility check: tokenization differences between v1.9 and v2.1 are minimal, but run token-embedding diff set.

Acceptance / rollback criteria (conservative):
- Must pass: error rate <= baseline + 0.1% (5xx, timeouts).
- Latency: p95 increase <= 10% vs baseline; p50 ideally improves but not required.
- Cost: per-token compute cost delta must be <= -5% (i.e., improvement) OR offset by improved latency.
- Quality: regression eval — using curated prompt set (eval/regression/canary-2024-11) must not show >2% degradation in task-specific metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) for top 10 intents.
- Observability: traces sampled at 100% for canary traffic for first 24h; token-level cost attributed.
- If any critical alert fires (model OOMs, spike in 5xx, model misbehavior flagged by safety monitor), immediate rollback to previous version and pause rollout.

Monitoring dashboard / alerts (quick links):
- Canary dashboard (WIP): /dash/rollouts/canary-v2.1 (add latency, errors, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens)
- SLOs: p99 < 2.5s for short requests (<=128 tokens).
- Alert thresholds (initial):
  - error_rate > baseline + 0.1% for 15m -> SEV2, auto-rollback if persists 30m.
  - p95 > baseline + 15% for 30m -> investigate (manual pause optional).
  - cost_increase > 10% for 24h -> pause and evaluate.

Runbook snippets:
- Quick rollback: update route defaultVersion -> redwood-model-v1.9 ; trigger rollout-service rollback API: POST /rollout/rollback {route:generate, to_version:v1.9} ; verify traffic returns to baseline and run smoke tests.
- Emergency: if OOM or GPU saturation, scale down v2.1 replicas to 0 via k8s and enable fallback routing to v1.9. Pager: oncall-sre@redwood.com, slack #sre-oncall.

Test plan (what to run during internal canary):
- Automated regression suite (nightly/regression/canary-smoke) with ~1k prompts (focus on top 25 intents).
- Human-in-the-loop spot checks: 20 prompts across categories (chat, summarization, code). Assign to: Jordan, Maya, Emma.
- Safety checks: run safety-scan against outputs (toxicity + policy detectors).
- Latency/cost microbench: p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost for 32/128/512 token lengths.

Checklist (todo items):
- [ ] Confirm infra capacity in us-west-2 dedicated pool (tickets: INF-789).
- [ ] Add canary dashboard widgets and 100% trace sampling for canary traffic.
- [ ] Create rollout config in rollout-service and add to infra repo (PR linked).
- [ ] Schedule internal canary start window (prefer low traffic, 02:00–08:00 PDT).
- [ ] Notify CS + enterprise customers with reserved capacity (heads-up e-mail).
- [ ] Prepare rollback PR and runbook in team repo.
- [ ] Run compatibility tokenization check and update tokenizer-mappings if needed.

Open questions / risks:
- Will v2.1's quantization path cause subtle semantic shifts for low-temperature generations? Need to run controlled prompts.
- Autoscaling interactions: when canary hits 25% we may need additional nodes; confirm autoscaler policy will prefer dedicated pool and not spin up mixed instances.
- Billing: dedicated pool usage vs hosted could shift cost attribution; check billing tags.

Notes to self (short):
- Keep canary small and measurable. Avoid chasing small latency wins if quality regressions appear.
- Remember to pin rollout window in calendar and set Slack reminders.
- If rollback, collect memory profiles and last-10-requests for debugging.

Snippets / commands (for quick copy):
- Create rollout config: ./scripts/create_rollout.sh --route generate --version v2.1 --initial-weight 0.01 --region us-west-2
- Rollback: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/rollout/rollback -d '{"route":"generate","to_version":"redwood-model-v1.9"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Check canary traffic: kubectl get hpa -n prod | grep generate-canary

End of scratchpad. Will extract to formal checklist + create PR once infra capacity confirmed.
